results.title: AWS GPU Price Increases 2026: What to Do About It
results.author: Kiril Urbonas
highlights:
EC2 Capacity Blocks went up around 15% in January and again in July. The increases track the memory shortage, and they change which GPU cloud is actually cheapest for your workload.

## Key takeaways

- AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block prices for ML twice in 2026, and as of October 2026 P6-B300 lists at $16.146 per accelerator-hour in us-east-1.
- Measure utilization per block before renewing, move portable training jobs to cheaper GPU clouds, and keep latency-sensitive inference where your data already lives.

...

AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block prices for ML in January and again on 1 July 2026, so re-run your GPU budget now. Measure utilization per block, split training from inference, price the portable training half at specialist clouds, and renew only blocks you keep above roughly 70% busy. Production inference inside AWS usually stays put.

...

Cloud compute prices go down. That has been the reliable direction for long enough that most capacity plans assume it implicitly. GPU capacity broke the pattern this year. Trade press put the January step at roughly 15% and the July step, which covered the P6-B300, P6-B200, P5, P5e, P5en and P4de families, at roughly 20%. If you budgeted accelerator spend in late 2025 and have not revisited it, your plan is wrong by a wide margin.

## The rates as of October 2026

These are the per-accelerator-hour Capacity Block rates on AWS's pricing page at the end of October 2026. Every instance has 8 accelerators, so multiply by 8 for the instance-hour.

| Instance | Accelerator | Region shown | Per accelerator-hour | Per instance-hour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | 8 x B300 | US East (N. Virginia) | $16.146 | $129.17 |
| P6-B200 | 8 x B200 | US East (N. Virginia) | $14.208 | $113.66 |
| P5en | 8 x H200 | US East (N. Virginia) | $7.895 | $63.16 |
| P5e | 8 x H200 | US East (Ohio) | $6.866 | $54.93 |
| P5 | 8 x H100 | US East (N. Virginia) | $5.970 | $47.76 |
| P4de | 8 x A100 | US East (N. Virginia) | $2.546 | $20.37 |

When we first wrote this in September, P6-B300 was about $14.04 and P6-B200 about $12.355, so the published rates have moved up roughly another 15% since. The page says prices are updated regularly based on supply and demand, that the next scheduled update is January 2027, and that you pay the rate in effect when you buy, even if the block starts after an update. That last point is the one to act on: if you know you need a block in Q1, buying it before January locks today's rate.

...

As far as we can tell, the increases are not a pricing experiment. They track the same component shortage that is repricing ordinary server memory, and accelerators are the sharp end of it. High-bandwidth memory sits on the accelerator package, and HBM is exactly what memory manufacturers have been redirecting fab capacity toward because it earns multiples of what conventional DDR5 earns. The result is that the scarce input is not the GPU die. It is the memory stacked next to it.

...

### How much does an AWS H100 Capacity Block cost?

As of October 2026, a P5 Capacity Block (8 x H100) lists at $5.970 per accelerator-hour in US East (N. Virginia), about $47.76 per instance-hour. H200-based P5en is $7.895, and Blackwell P6-B200 is $14.208. You pay the rate in effect when you purchase, and AWS's next scheduled price update is January 2027.

results.title: AI Price Hikes 2026: The 10 Nobody Warned You About
results.author: Capital, Compute
highlights:
## 5. Nvidia told its biggest customers AI servers cost more than 15 percent extra

Nvidia notified its largest customers that prices of servers containing its AI chips are rising more than 15 percent in many cases, with increases taking effect on systems shipped early next year and covering the flagship Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell generations. It was first reported by Bloomberg on 22 August 2026 and confirmed in Fortune’s reporting citing people familiar with the process. The stated cause is soaring memory chip costs.

...

## 2. Graphics cards absorbed three kit hikes in seven months

Nvidia passed memory costs to board partners three times in 2026. TrendForce reported January at 10 to 15 percent, with 16GB-and-above models at 15 to 20 percent. May was narrow and hit the RTX 5090 line only. Late July was the broad one at 20 to 30 percent, reaching every GeForce RTX model.

Those compound. A mid-range card that missed the May increase is roughly 32 to 50 percent more expensive than in January, before a retailer adds anything. An Asus TUF RTX 5080 went from $1,199 to $1,595, or 33 percent, which sits at the bottom of that band. The unabsorbed remainder is the risk to anyone waiting. Full chain in GPU prices in 2026, with current levels on the GPU price tracker.

results.title: AI算力需求强劲，亚马逊云业务再次上调GPU服务价格 - 黄金交易平台 - 投资资讯
highlights:
# AI算力需求强劲，亚马逊云业务再次上调GPU服务价格 

 2026-11-15 01:23:29 阅读量 投资资讯 

亚马逊(AMZN.US)旗下的算力上调云计算服务AWS宣布，自7月1日起，需求逊将其机器学习专用EC2 Capacity Blocks的强劲容量预留服务价格上调，涵盖多款搭载英伟达(NVDA.US) GPU的亚马业务实例。这是再次AWS自年初以来再次进行价格调整，表明AI算力需求依然旺盛。算力上调

AWS指出，需求逊此次涨价主要涉及P6-B300、强劲P6-B200、亚马业务P5、再次P5e、算力上调P5en和P4de等实例类型。需求逊其中，强劲 P6-B300和P6-B200使用英伟达的亚马业务Blackwell B300和B200 GPU，而P5系列使用H100和H200 GPU，再次P4系列则配备A100 GPU。

根据最新定价，P6-B300实例的每块GPU小时费用提高至14.04美元，P6-B200涨至12.355美元；P5实例在美国的价格升至5.191美元，非美国地区为4.72美元；P5e和P5en的价格同步上调，而P4de的价格则提高到每块GPU每小时约2.214美元。

AWS还表示，其余服务的价格未做改变，并将根据市场供需情况对EC2 Capacity Blocks机器学习容量预留服务的价格进行定期调整。

分析认为，此次调整再次反映出AI算力资源的供不应求。随着生成式AI、大语言模型以及智能体的迅速发展，对GPU算力的需求持续上升。此外，英伟达的H100、H200及最新的Blackwell系列GPU长期短缺，推动云服务提供商调整租赁价格。

AWS公布的价格还显示，搭载72颗Blackwell GB200 GPU的P6e UltraServer在美国达拉斯地区的每小时租赁费用高达761.9美元，相当于每块GPU每小时约10.58美元。

此外，搭载8颗H100 GPU的P5实例在主要地区的每小时租赁费用约为34.61美元；8颗H200 GPU的P5en实例约为45.77美元；而包含8颗A100 GPU的P4系列实例每小时租赁价格在11.8美元至14.77美元不等。

results.title: CoreWeave pricing in 2026: every GPU rate explained
results.author: Lyne Carolyne
highlights:
Quick Answer

CoreWeave, a GPU cloud provider, prices start at $6.16 per GPU hour for an Nvidia H100 and reaches $8.60 for a B200, sold as fixed multi-GPU nodes: an 8x H100 node lists at $49.24 per hour on demand. Spot rates run up to 60 percent below on demand, reserved contracts discount up to 60 percent, and egress is free.

In April 2026, CoreWeave filed an 8-K with the SEC disclosing an expanded agreement with Meta: approximately $21 billion for AI cloud capacity through December 2032, deployed across multiple locations and including some of the first Nvidia Vera Rubin systems, per the filing.

...

Your commitment will start where Meta’s negotiators started, though: a public rate card that prices by the node and discounts up to 60 percent behind closed doors.

...

On-demand GPU nodes run from $10.00 per hour for an 8x L40 to $68.80 for an 8x B200, with the workhorse 8x H100 node at $49.24. Every figure on the public card prices a full instance, not a chip, so the CoreWeave price you’ll actually compare against other clouds takes one extra division.

Here are CoreWeave’s North America rates as of 2026, normalized per GPU:

| GPU (instance config) | On demand, node/hr | Per GPU/hr | Spot, node/hr | Inference single GPU/hr |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nvidia HGX H100 (8x) | $49.24 | $6.16 | $19.71 | $6.16 |
| Nvidia HGX H200 (8x) | $50.44 | $6.31 | $20.93 | $6.31 |
| Nvidia HGX B200 (8x) | $68.80 | $8.60 | $34.11 | $8.60 |
| Nvidia GB200 NVL72 (4 GPU) | $42.00 | $10.50 | N/A | $10.50 |
| Nvidia HGX B300 (8x) | Contact sales | N/A | $35.84 | N/A |
| Nvidia GB300 NVL72 (4 GPU) | Contact sales | N/A | N/A | N/A |
| Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, high memory (8x) | $20.00 | $2.50 | $11.09 | $2.50 |
| Nvidia GH200 (1x) | $6.50 | $6.50 | N/A | $6.50 |
| Nvidia A100 80GB (8x) | $21.60 | $2.70 | $9.65 | $2.70 |
| Nvidia L40S (8x) | $18.00 | $2.25 | $7.88 | $2.25 |
| Nvidia L40 (8x) | $10.00 | $1.25 | $6.27 | $1.25 |

Note: GB200 and GB300 instances bundle two Grace Blackwell Superchips, four GPUs total. The inference column applies only to CoreWeave inference platform customers. European spot rates differ slightly: the H100 node runs $19.51 there versus $19.71 in North America.

...

You can buy CoreWeave compute three ways: on demand by the hour, spot at up to 60 percent off with interruption risk, and reserved capacity under negotiated multi-year contracts discounted up to 60 percent. The rate card shows the first two. The CoreWeave business model runs on the third.

No public term-rate table exists for reserved capacity. Where Google Cloud publishes its committed-use discounts in full, CoreWeave publishes a ceiling and routes you to sales. The Meta and OpenAI agreements are that tier at its extreme, and they tell you who the rate card is really for: everyone who hasn’t negotiated yet.

...

Blackwell landed on the public rate card. The 8x B200 node lists at $68.80 per hour with an $8.60 single GPU inference rate, the GB200 NVL72 instance at $42.00, and B300-class hardware shows spot pricing while on-demand buyers still go through sales, the usual tell for supply-constrained chips.

results.title: Nvidia raised prices on Microsoft, Google and Oracle. | Enrico Sieni
results.author: Enrico Sieni
highlights:
# Nvidia raised prices on Microsoft, Google and Oracle. | Enrico Sieni · LinkedIn · 2026-09-11T00:00:00+00:00

**Enrico Sieni**: Pricing Strategy Expert | Helping Mid-Market Companies ($10MM-$1Bn) Increase EBITDA 200-800 bps Through Strategic Pricing | Co-Founder @ Revify Analytics.

---

Nvidia raised prices on Microsoft, Google and Oracle.

AI systems shipping in early 2027 will cost more than 15% more. Memory chip prices went vertical this year and Nvidia decided not to absorb it.

That part is ordinary. The interesting part is that Nvidia runs a 75% gross margin. It could have swallowed the whole increase and no customer would have felt a thing. It passed the cost through anyway, and it did it four to five months ahead, privately, account by account, before any of it reached the press.

That notice window does two jobs. The customer has time to get the number into next year's budget, and you hear the pushback while there is still time to act on it, instead of after the invoice arrives.

Most B2B suppliers run this in reverse. They quietly eat the cost for a few quarters, then send a letter 30 days out. The increase reads as a surprise, so the customer argues about the number rather than planning around it.

results.title: Nvidia’s Four-Year-Old H100 Sees Rental Prices Surge 22% in a Month
results.author: Chosun Ilbo
highlights:
## At a glance

 News Named sources Ongoing story 

- Cloud rental prices for Nvidia’s H100 AI accelerator, released in September 2022, rose 21.89% over the past month.
- Demand has spread to the four-year-old chip as supplies of newer AI accelerators fail to keep pace with demand.
- AI computing financial trading platform Ornn reported the increase on Sept. 7 local time.

Nvidia’s H100 AI accelerator is four years old, but its rental price is moving in the opposite direction from its age.

Cloud rental prices for the H100 rose 21.89% in the past month, according to AI computing financial trading platform Ornn. Nvidia released the accelerator in September 2022.

Demand for older products has increased because supplies of newer AI accelerators have failed to keep up with demand. As a result, users are also turning to the H100 for AI computing capacity.

Nvidia’s H100 SXM is now an older comparison part, with 80GB of HBM3 and roughly 3.35 TB/s of memory bandwidth per Nvidia’s own published specifications. On the GPU marketplace Spheron, H100-class capacity has traded in the low single digits per hour depending on provider and commitment. The B200, built on the Blackwell architecture, is also an older generation now. It carries 192GB of HBM3e (matching Ironwood’s per-chip capacity) and roughly 8 TB/s of bandwidth. The B300 and GB300 appeared in October 2026 rental coverage, with on-demand B300 rental reportedly $7.10 to $17.80 per GPU-hour across public cloud providers and GB300 reportedly $10.42 to $18.00 per GPU-hour across two providers, so prices vary widely by provider. Nvidia’s newest architecture is now Vera Rubin, which reached general availability with CUDA 13.5 on November 4, 2026, and this comparison lists no rental prices for it.

...

On the Nvidia side, B300 and GB300 are presented as currently rentable products in October 2026, which makes H100 and B200 older comparison products relative to them. The same October 2026 coverage says NVIDIA publishes no purchase list price, so retail pricing or reseller estimates should not be described as official NVIDIA list prices.

...

| Chip | Memory | Bandwidth | On-Demand Price | Availability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Google TPU v7 Ironwood | 192GB HBM3e | ~7.37 TB/s | $12.00/hr (Iowa) | Google Cloud only |
| Nvidia H100 SXM | 80GB HBM3 | ~3.35 TB/s | ~$2.69-3.00/hr (aggregator avg.) | Multi-cloud, widely resold |
| Nvidia B200 SXM6 | 192GB HBM3e | ~8 TB/s | $11.28/hr on-demand (September 2026) | Multi-cloud marketplaces |
| AMD MI300X | 192GB HBM3 | ~5.3 TB/s | Varies by provider, not uniformly published | Microsoft, Meta and select clouds |

...

A few things look likely to play out over the next two to three quarters. First, expect Nvidia’s cloud partners to respond to Ironwood’s published committed-use rates with more aggressive multi-year discounting of their own, especially on B200 and Blackwell-generation capacity, to keep price-sensitive customers from evaluating a Google Cloud migration. Second, Google will likely keep negotiating below-list rates for anchor customers like Anthropic even with a public price sheet now in place, since the $1.60-per-hour reported rate shows how much room Google has to discount for volume without touching its published numbers.
